    What this tool does

    HEIC is the format an iPhone shoots in since iOS 11. It is genuinely better technology — half the size of a JPG with more dynamic range — and it is also the reason a photo you texted to a colleague turns into a blank icon on Windows, is refused by a job portal and will not open in an older version of Office. Converting to JPG is the two-second fix, and it needs to happen on your side before the file leaves your hands.

    This page decodes HEIC in the browser with a pinned, integrity-checked decoder that streams down only when you actually pick a HEIC file. The photo is decoded to pixels, re-encoded as standard JPEG with your quality setting, and offered back as a download. Nothing is uploaded: the raw HEIC never leaves the tab, which is worth something when the pictures are family photos, scanned documents or anything you would not post to a free conversion site.

    iPhone HEIC files carry rotation metadata and, on newer models, depth and edit stacks. Rotation is applied here so the JPG is upright the way you took it; the extra computational-photography data is not preserved, because JPG cannot carry it. Live Photos convert from their still frame. Batch a whole album if you like — the status line counts through each file, and Download all as ZIP puts the set back into one archive.

    How to use the HEIC to JPG | Step by Step Guide

    1. Drop .heic or .heif files into the box — from Downloads, or AirDrop them to your Mac first.
    2. Choose JPG (default) or PNG output, then set quality for the size you need.
    3. Press Convert to JPG. The first run downloads the decoder, so it pauses briefly.
    4. Save each photo from the grid, or grab one ZIP for the whole batch.
    5. Share the JPG anywhere: WhatsApp, email, CNIC or visa portals, Word.

    Features

    • Real HEIC decoding inside the browser, no upload and no server queue
    • EXIF rotation honoured, so portrait shots stay portrait
    • Quality control for the JPEG, plus an optional PNG output
    • Batch conversion with progress counting and one ZIP

    Tips

    • On iPhone, Settings > Camera > Formats > Most Compatible makes future shots JPG if you would rather not convert at all.
    • Files shared through WhatsApp are already converted by iPhone; email and AirDrop are the ones that keep HEIC.
    • A HEIC that refuses to decode is usually a raw Pro or a file from a very new iOS build — screenshot it or export it as JPG from the Photos app.
    • Faces look best around quality 85; below 70 skin tones start to band.
    • Convert once. Every later JPG save costs detail the HEIC originally had.

    Frequently asked questions

    Is the heic to jpg free to use?

    Yes — HEIC to JPG has no usage cap, no sign-up and no watermark, and it is not a trial: the page is a static file on https://wafasmart.tech with no billing backend behind it. iPhone owners can convert an entire album without a subscription.

    Does anything get uploaded when I use heic to jpg?

    No. HEIC to JPG reads your HEIC photo straight into page memory, works on it locally and hands the result back as a download — there is no upload request to intercept, store or leak, and no log of what you processed.

    Why does the first conversion take a few seconds?

    The HEIC decoder is deliberately not bundled with the page — it streams from a pinned CDN the first time a HEIC file is picked, then your browser caches it for the rest of the session.

    Does quality drop when I convert?

    HEIC to JPG is a lossy re-encode, so some detail is traded away. At quality 85 the difference is hard to see on a phone screen; keep the original HEIC if you plan to edit.

    Can it convert Live Photos?

    The still image of a Live Photo converts. The short video half is a separate MOV file and is not part of this tool.

    Does it work on Android and Windows?

    Yes, in any modern browser — the constraint is the file, not the operating system. Save the HEIC to your device first, then drop it in.

    Should I process sensitive family photos and document scans here?

    Because nothing leaves the tab, HEIC to JPG is a reasonable choice for CNICs, payslips and bank statements. Two habits add safety: close the tab afterwards so page memory is released, and keep the original file — editing produces a new document rather than modifying the one you own.
